source: Based on the topics of the Armenian grade 7 mathematics textbooks

stages.headline: Two expressions are identically equal if their values agree for every value of the variables; such an equality is an identity.
stages.headlineEnglish: Two expressions are identically equal if their values agree for every value of the variables; such an equality is an identity.

stages.headline: To prove an identity, transform one side until it becomes the other, or bring both to the same form.
stages.headlineEnglish: To prove an identity, transform one side until it becomes the other, or bring both to the same form.

stages.headline: To show an equality is not an identity, one value where it fails is enough.
stages.headlineEnglish: To show an equality is not an identity, one value where it fails is enough.

optionsQuiz.feedbackIncorrect: 🤔 Not quite. The correct answer is {correctText}.

stages.headline: Prove the identity (x + 3)(x − 1) = x² + 2x − 3.
stages.solutionSteps: 1. The left side expands to the right side.
stages.solutionStepsEnglish: 1. The left side expands to the right side.
stages.customInstructions: The student must expand the left side and show it equals the right side.

stages.headline: Show that (a − b)² = a² − b² is not an identity.
stages.headlineEnglish: Show that (a − b)² = a² − b² is not an identity.
stages.problemText: Show that (a − b)² = a² − b² is not an identity.
stages.customInstructions: Any correct counterexample (values where the sides differ) is accepted.

stages.headline: Find k so that 3(x + k) = 3x + 12 is an identity.
stages.headlineEnglish: Find k so that 3(x + k) = 3x + 12 is an identity.
stages.problemText: Find k so that 3(x + k) = 3x + 12 is an identity.
